# Cookbook: using `delphi` on a repository that already exists

**This file is generated by running it.** `cookbook.mjs` ran every command below in a checkout of
[github.com/fractastical/morpholib](https://github.com/fractastical/morpholib) at commit `befd35cd` (2026-11-22) and pasted what
came back. The store that run produced is in [`cookbook/nodes.jsonl`](cookbook/nodes.jsonl), and
`node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --check` recomputes it and confirms every node id printed here is in it.

**The question the recipes answer:** three Lean files in that repository each say they contain no
`sorry`. Is that true, and could a stranger have checked it from the files?

**What the run found:** yes, and no. All 115 theorems and lemmas are accepted by the Lean kernel on its
three standard axioms. None of the three files could show that as published, because none asks Lean to
print the axioms its theorems depend on. One line per theorem fixes it.

Nothing was pushed to that repository and nothing of it is redistributed here beyond the one line in
each file that states the claim. In the commands below, `delphi` is `node tracks/kernel/embed/delphi.mjs`.

## 1. Adopt it

One command, run at the top of the existing repository. It adds a `.delphi/` folder and changes nothing else.

```console
$ delphi init --name morpholib
initialised  .delphi
project      morpholib
store        .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl  (append-only, one record per line, commit it)
method       .delphi/BEST_PRACTICES.md  (generated; regenerate with `delphi best-practices`)
graph        .delphi/graph/index.html   (rewritten after every mint, private to this project)
laws         .delphi/laws/              (put your Lean files here)

Next: record the source of one number you already rely on.
  delphi evidence --kind doi --ref <doi> --quote "<the words it prints>" --where "<table or section>"

Lean files are checked by the checker that ships beside the kernel, which needs a Lean 4
toolchain on this machine. Without one, `delphi law --lean` is refused as unchecked, never
passed. A law given with --script instead says on its record that a script checked it.
```

## 2. Record what the project claims, in its own words

Evidence is a source and the exact words read in it. Here the source is a file in the repository
itself, and the words are the line where it states its claim. A fact is the number in that sentence,
filed under that evidence, with the conditions that pin it down: which file, at which commit.

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean --quote "in pure core Lean 4 (zero external dependencies, zero `sorry`s, sub-second kernel check)." --where "line 8, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c  file:morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement "MathOfBiology.lean states that it contains no sorry" --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition "file=morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean" --condition "commit=befd35cd" --evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c
fact     kdcbf9d1df9057817  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

The other two files are recorded the same way:

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean --quote "Kernel-check (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms, no Mathlib):" --where "line 10, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k8d1011f43d5f7fc6  file:morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement "Ruliobiology.lean states that it contains no sorry" --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition "file=morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean" --condition "commit=befd35cd" --evidence k8d1011f43d5f7fc6
fact     k628b6f9ff55fd9b6  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

```console
$ delphi evidence --kind file --ref morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean --quote "(0 sorry, no additional axioms). STATUS: PROTOTYPE — not yet emitted into the KG." --where "line 7, the file's header comment" --retrieved 2026-11-22
evidence k7b5041a927d1e37c  file:morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
```

```console
$ delphi fact --statement "LinearResource.lean states that it contains no sorry" --quantity sorry_claimed --value 0 --unit count --condition "file=morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean" --condition "commit=befd35cd" --evidence k7b5041a927d1e37c
fact     k10511a275f5fa506  sorry_claimed = 0 count
```

**Notice:** try leaving out `--quote`, or `--condition`. The command refuses and says which rule it
broke. That refusal is the method working, not the tool being awkward.

## 3. Ask the kernel to accept the claim as published

```console
$ delphi law --name MathOfBiology_as_published --informal "Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom." --lean morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
REFUSED  law MathOfBiology_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean has 76 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

The same for the other two:

```console
$ delphi law --name Ruliobiology_as_published --informal "Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom." --lean morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
REFUSED  law Ruliobiology_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean has 31 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

```console
$ delphi law --name LinearResource_as_published --informal "Every theorem in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel with no sorry and no added axiom." --lean morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
REFUSED  law LinearResource_as_published
         - morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean has 8 theorem(s) and no "#print axioms" line: nothing in it can be audited
```

**Notice:** this is not a failed proof. The kernel refused before starting Lean, because a file with
no `#print axioms` line gives nothing to audit: a hand-written `axiom` would pass every search for
`sorry`. "Zero sorry" was true here and unverifiable, which is the common case.

## 4. Make it checkable without touching it

`delphi audit` copies the file into `.delphi/laws/` and appends one audit line per theorem. The
original is only read. Then `delphi law` runs Lean on the copy and records what it printed.

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean  sha256 2907c36ca2c36fcd
         76 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 76 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name MathOfBiology_audited --informal "Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom." --lean MathOfBiology.Audited.lean
law      k2d8d7e578a17676d  MathOfBiology_audited
         .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  76 declaration(s) audited
```

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean  sha256 79d470f8eb339b95
         31 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 31 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/Ruliobiology.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name Ruliobiology_audited --informal "Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom." --lean Ruliobiology.Audited.lean
law      k9132887d6adcec44  Ruliobiology_audited
         .delphi/laws/Ruliobiology.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  31 declaration(s) audited
```

```console
$ delphi audit morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean
audit    morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean  sha256 94741a6acae4c1cc
         8 theorem(s) and lemma(s), 0 axiom-audit line(s) as published, 0 sorry in code, 0 hand-written axiom(s), 0 import(s)
         copy with 8 audit line(s) appended -> .delphi/laws/LinearResource.Audited.lean  (the original was only read)
```

```console
$ delphi law --name LinearResource_audited --informal "Every theorem and lemma in this file is accepted by the Lean kernel on its three standard axioms, with no sorry and no hand-written axiom." --lean LinearResource.Audited.lean
law      kcaa376871942f6a4  LinearResource_audited
         .delphi/laws/LinearResource.Audited.lean  CHECKED  axioms [Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]  8 declaration(s) audited
```

**Notice:** each law record carries the hash of the exact bytes Lean checked. Edit the file afterwards
and `delphi doctor` will say the record no longer matches.

## 5. Apply the law to the claim

A verdict is a law applied to facts. The check here is a twelve-line script kept in the project, so
anyone can read what "inside" meant:

```js
// Is the file's own claim true of the file? Inside when the code holds exactly as many `sorry` as it
// claims and no hand-written axiom. The Lean kernel's acceptance is the law this is applied under;
// this script only counts, so that the verdict names numbers a reader can recount.
import fs from 'node:fs';

export default (values, facts) => {
  const file = facts[0].conditions.file;
  const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
  const code = src.replace(/\/-[\s\S]*?-\//g, ' ').replace(/--[^\n]*/g, ' ');
  const sorry = (code.match(/\bsorry\b/g) ?? []).length;
  const axioms = (code.match(/^\s*axiom\s+/gm) ?? []).length;
  return {
    result: sorry === values.sorry_claimed && axioms === 0 ? 'inside' : 'outside',
    detail: `${file}: ${sorry} sorry in code against ${values.sorry_claimed} claimed, ${axioms} hand-written axiom(s)`,
  };
};
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k2d8d7e578a17676d --fact kdcbf9d1df9057817 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label "MathOfBiology: the zero-sorry claim"
verdict  k1e4d15121973226f  INSIDE  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k9132887d6adcec44 --fact k628b6f9ff55fd9b6 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label "Ruliobiology: the zero-sorry claim"
verdict  kb51caeb94192b4c6  INSIDE  Ruliobiology_audited [Ruliobiology: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/Ruliobiology.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

```console
$ delphi verdict --law kcaa376871942f6a4 --fact k10511a275f5fa506 --requires sorry_claimed --check .delphi/checks/claim-matches-file.mjs --label "LinearResource: the zero-sorry claim"
verdict  kc889878ccaef6613  INSIDE  LinearResource_audited [LinearResource: the zero-sorry claim]
         morphoeval/lean/LinearResource.lean: 0 sorry in code against 0 claimed, 0 hand-written axiom(s)
```

The first file's header also says its kernel check is sub-second. Nobody has recorded a timing, so
the honest answer is neither yes nor no:

```console
$ delphi verdict --law k2d8d7e578a17676d --fact kdcbf9d1df9057817 --requires kernel_check_seconds --expr "kernel_check_seconds < 1" --label "MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim"
verdict  kcc2a658ba4df8e79  CANNOT-ASSESS  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim]
         missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
         cannot-assess is not a pass. A build resting on this will be refused.
```

**Notice:** `cannot-assess` is a result, never a pass. In most codebases a check with a missing input
returns true.

## 6. Build something, or be told exactly why not

An artifact resting on the unassessed claim is refused, and the refusal is itself recorded:

```console
$ delphi build --artifact "a \"checks in under a second\" badge" --verdict kcc2a658ba4df8e79
REFUSED  a "checks in under a second" badge
         - MathOfBiology_audited (MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim): could not be assessed — missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds

The refusal is itself a record: ka76c8b9868c534e6. It is the shortest list of what would have to
be true for this artifact to be honest, so it is worth publishing rather than hiding.
```

An artifact resting on the three verdicts that held is minted, and its file is hashed into the record:

```console
$ delphi build --artifact "axiom audit report" --verdict k1e4d15121973226f --verdict kb51caeb94192b4c6 --verdict kc889878ccaef6613 --file delphi-audit/REPORT.md
build    k32662bbfff6c00d2  axiom audit report
         0f285b72234c7349      1006  delphi-audit/REPORT.md
```

## 7. Read it back

Anything in the store can be walked back to the words it rests on:

```console
$ delphi why badge
refusal  ka76c8b9868c534e6  a "checks in under a second" badge
         - MathOfBiology_audited (MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim): could not be assessed — missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
  verdict  kcc2a658ba4df8e79  CANNOT-ASSESS  MathOfBiology_audited [MathOfBiology: the sub-second claim]  missing input(s): kernel_check_seconds
    fact     kdcbf9d1df9057817  sorry_claimed = 0 count  [file=morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean, commit=befd35cd]
      evidence k8385c2c983dc1c4c  file:morphoeval/lean/MathOfBiology.lean  "in pure core Lean 4 (zero external dependencies, zero `sorry`s, sub-second kern…"  (line 8, the file's header comment)
    law      k2d8d7e578a17676d  MathOfBiology_audited  .delphi/laws/MathOfBiology.Audited.lean -> CHECKED axioms[Classical.choice, Quot.sound, propext]
```

```console
$ delphi summary
store    .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl
nodes    15  (3 evidence, 3 fact, 3 law, 4 verdict, 1 refusal, 1 build)
verdicts 3 inside, 0 outside, 1 cannot-assess
builds   1 minted, 1 refused
chain    every id and link recomputed clean
```

## 8. Put two commands in CI

`verify` recomputes every id and chain link. `doctor` checks what can rot without anyone touching the
store: a proof file edited after it was accepted, an artifact regenerated without a new build, a check
that has answered nothing twice.

```console
$ delphi verify
verified 15 node(s): every id matches its content and every chain link holds
```

```console
$ delphi doctor
note     1 refusal(s) on record. These are the most useful thing in the store to publish: `delphi why <name>` prints what each one was missing.
doctor: 15 node(s) sound — store chain, 3 proof file(s), 1 artifact file(s) all match their recorded hashes; 1 note(s)
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/delphi.yml
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  record:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20 }
      - run: node path/to/delphi.mjs verify
      - run: node path/to/delphi.mjs doctor
```

## What this run does not say

- It does not say the theorems are the **right** theorems. A statement can be accepted by the kernel
  and say nothing: contradictory hypotheses prove anything. That needs a reader.
- It does not say a formal statement matches the biology it is named after.
- The axioms listed are the bound every audited theorem was confirmed to be within, which is what the
  checker reports, not a per-theorem list.
- It was run once, on one commit. The commit is named above so the run can be repeated against it.

## Run it yourself

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1 https://github.com/fractastical/morpholib
cd morpholib && git sparse-checkout init --no-cone && git sparse-checkout set '/morphoeval/lean/*' && git checkout
node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --repo /path/to/morpholib   # needs a Lean 4 toolchain
node tracks/kernel/embed/cookbook.mjs --check                     # needs nothing
```

The graph this run produced, as a page: [`cookbook/graph.html`](cookbook/graph.html).
